Unified MPCurve fit object

Source: R/MPCurver-package.R
mpcurve.Rd

The public return type of fit_mpcurve and do_mpcurve. An mpcurve object normalizes the public fields of the recommended CAVI backend while retaining the raw fit in $fit.

Single-ordering objects

For intrinsic_dim = 1, $params$pi is a length-K position-prior vector, $params$mu is a d x K posterior-mean trajectory matrix, $params$sigma2 is a length-d estimated variance vector (or NULL when measurement standard deviations are supplied through S), and $gamma is the n x K responsibility matrix. The full Gaussian trajectory posterior is available from $fit$posterior. When S is supplied, $measurement_sd stores either its length-d feature-shared form or its n x d observation-level form.

Fixed-M structural partition objects

For intrinsic_dim = M >= 2, the variational family is $$q(C)\prod_{j=1}^d q(Z_j)q(U_j\mid Z_j).$$ The normalized object has one canonical structural state:

  • $params$pi: named list of M length-K position-prior vectors;

  • $params$mu: named list of M d x K conditional posterior-mean matrices;

  • $params$sigma2: one shared length-d estimated variance vector, or NULL for known measurement noise;

  • $gamma: named list of M n x K position-responsibility matrices;

  • $measurement_sd: NULL when noise is estimated, or the supplied length-d / n x d known-standard-deviation specification;

  • $conditional_posterior: named conditional Gaussian state for \(q(U_j\mid Z_j=m)\). Each $mean[[m]] is d x K; each $cov[[m]][[j]] is K x K; and $var[[m]] (also available as $diag[[m]]) is d x K;

  • $lambda_mat: a d x M matrix of smoothness parameters;

  • $partition$pi_weights: a d x M matrix containing \(q(Z_j=m)\), with the hard display assignment in $partition$assign;

  • $objective_history and $temperature_history: the fixed-M structural objective and its temperature schedule. Objective values at different temperatures are not directly comparable; use the exact \(T=1\) segment for monotonicity checks.

$fits contains named, derived single-ordering views for compatibility with existing inspection and plotting code. Those views are not independent fitting states and are never used to continue the structural algorithm. Structural objects always retain their requested fixed M; the compatibility fields $active_intrinsic_dim and $displayed_intrinsic_dim therefore both equal M.
